claim_scope: Candidate C9c-4. This packet declared 22 mechanical rows and only 18 distinct mutations: four rows repeated three mutations verbatim, inflating the count the replay gate checks. The distinctness rule this same candidate added to the ledger grader (Opus P40 P2-1) is what caught it, on its first real run, against my own evidence. The duplicates are dropped; every distinct mutation still kills. (opus2 P40 P2-2/P2-3) The killer grammar gains one form: <crate>/src/<file>.rs::<filter>, run as cargo test --lib. It exists because a guard whose only honest test is a crate unit test -- the check it protects is private, and no accepted object can reach it from an integration test -- could otherwise carry no mechanical row at all, which is exactly how a Rust guard shipped with a test that never called it. The hygiene validator accepts a pinned crate source as a killer path for the same reason. What is NOT claimed: that a lib killer is as tightly bound as an integration one; a filter selects by test-name substring across the whole crate, and the control run's 'something actually ran' guard is what keeps an empty selection from qualifying a mutant. PREDECESSOR: v3 (Opus P38 P2-5, P2-6, P3): the ledger is now EXECUTED BY THE PACKET (two replay commands run it over the packets carrying mechanical rows and grade the report: every mechanical row killed, none survived, none errored, the count pinned), where before ninety-two mechanical rows were gated by nothing and executed only by hand. A row could also read as KILLED without the DESCRIBED mutation being the one that mattered, because the report recorded only the mutated file's digest; each row now records the mutation itself (path, needle and replacement digests, the needle's first line). The pytest control gains the cargo path's guard that at least one test actually ran. Earlier: v3 (Opus P38 P2-5, P2-6, P3): the ledger is now EXECUTED BY THE PACKET (two replay commands run it over the packets carrying mechanical rows and grade the report: every mechanical row killed, none survived, none errored, the count pinned), where before ninety-two mechanical rows were gated by nothing and executed only by hand. A row could also read as KILLED without the DESCRIBED mutation being the one that mattered, because the report recorded only the mutated file's digest; each row now records the mutation itself (path, needle and replacement digests, the needle's first line). The pytest control gains the cargo path's guard that at least one test actually ran. Earlier: v2 (integrator, C9c-1): the added-packet rule that refuses string-only rows now exempts a packet only when BOTH its evidence-id date and its own created_date precede the cutover. Membership of the diff cannot be the key on its own: a diff against the campaign base reports every packet cut since then as ADDED, including ones authored before the cutover whose append-only rows may not be re-cut, which made the deep hygiene gate unsatisfiable; reading created_date keeps the rule's teeth against a back-dated evidence id, and an unreadable or absent date is treated as post-cutover so a packet that will not say when it was authored does not earn the exemption. DECLARED RESIDUAL, in the function docstring: a packet that back-dates BOTH fields is exempt, because nothing in the evidence directory records when a packet was authored. Earlier: v1 (M1 / P3, item 01): tools/thv1_mutation_ledger_v1.py executes every mechanical mutation row of a test-hygiene packet in a fresh git-archive copy (pins checked against the copy, needle exactly once, killer green on an unmutated control copy and red on the mutated copy: pytest exit 1 or a cargo FAILED summary; a killer that still passes marks the row SURVIVED and the ledger exits 1; narrative rows are listed and never counted). tools/test_hygiene_evidence_v1.py closes the row schema to mechanical {description, killed_by, mutant: {path, needle, replacement}} with the path among the source pins and the killer a pinned pytest node or a pinned cargo test filter, or narrative {description, killed_by, narrative: true}; string-only rows survive only in packets dated before 20260903 as legacy replay records that no gate ever executed. tools/check_test_hygiene_v1.py counts rows by kind, verifies the needle count on every current pin, and refuses an added packet with legacy rows whatever its date. This packet's own rows are mechanical and executed by the ledger on itself. Research-only evidence; authority NONE; formal_core_complete stays false.

nonclaims: The mutation ledger executes declared rows only; it does not measure mutants nobody declared.
A green ledger says nothing about code no row names; it makes the packet's mutation claims honest, not complete.
The ledger runs no Lean, verifies no receipts, mounts nothing, and raises no authority.
Legacy string-only rows in packets dated before 20260903 remain unexecuted historical records; the checker reports their count and nothing more.
